sheet-4-1.description: The upper strip of sheet 4 covers the northern end of Glen Ridge along the Montclair line, drawn at the small scale of 200 feet to an inch. Ridgewood Avenue runs the length of the strip, with Broad Street below it, and Bay Avenue crosses the left end, where Highland Avenue comes in at the top left corner and Sherman, Forest and Essex Avenues end against it. Oxford Street runs from Ridgewood Avenue up to Walnut Crescent at the top, and the Montclair town line, lettered with a note to see volume three, runs across the top margin. The Glen Ridge borough line crosses the strip diagonally. The ground is almost entirely open: large tracts are lettered with the names of their owners rather than divided into lots, among them the William T. Evans property with its stone house and outbuildings between Bay Avenue and Oxford Street, smaller holdings of W. T. Evans along Bay Avenue, the James N. Jarvie tract in the middle of the strip and the Henry Lindenmeyer estate towards the right. The club house of the Glen Ridge Golf Club stands beside Oxford Street. Only a handful of buildings are drawn, scattered stables and dwellings on the large holdings. Water pipes are marked in Bay Avenue, Sherman, Forest and Essex Avenues and Broad Street, and a fire alarm box at the junction of Bay Avenue and Broad Street. Block numbers 1 to 5 and the numbers of adjoining sheets (12 along Bay Avenue, 4 for the lower strip) are printed in the margins.
notes: Drawn at 200 feet to an inch.
Large holdings lettered William T. Evans, W. T. Evans, James N. Jarvie and Henry Lindenmeyer Est.
Glen Ridge Golf Club club house beside Oxford Street.
Sherman Avenue is drawn only as a stub west of Bay Avenue; it did not yet reach Oxford Street.
All control lies along Bay Avenue at the left end of the strip; the right end is placed by extrapolation along Ridgewood Avenue (leave-one-out about 9 m).

North end of Glen Ridge at the Montclair line, 200 ft to an inch. Two parts separated by a heavy horizontal line: part 1 (top) Ridgewood Av, Broad St, Bay Av, Oxford St, Essex Av, Forest Av, Sherman Av (W. T. Evans estate, Jarvie and Lindenmeyer estates); part 2 (bottom) Ridgewood Av, Broad St, Watchung Av, Dodd St, Gray St (large estates).

sheet-4-2.description: The lower strip of sheet 4, below a heavy dividing line, continues the northern end of Glen Ridge at 200 feet to an inch. Ridgewood Avenue runs across the top of the strip from Dodd Street and Gray Street, which run up to the Montclair town line, to Watchung Avenue on the right; Broad Street runs along the bottom edge, and Watchung Avenue crosses diagonally from Ridgewood Avenue down to Broad Street, following the Glen Ridge borough line for part of its length. The town line of Montclair, with a note to see volume three, runs along the top. Between Ridgewood Avenue and Broad Street the ground is divided into long narrow holdings running back from Broad Street, each lettered with its owner's name: the Henry Lindenmeyer estate, H. O. Van Giesen, T. B. Baxter, S. J. Dodd, B. Coyne, C. Callin, J. R. Gibson, Philip Baum, J. Miller and Beyer Brothers. They are almost empty, with only small dwellings and stables near the Broad Street frontage and a few buildings along Watchung Avenue. The Glen Ridge borough line crosses the strip diagonally. A twelve-inch water main is drawn in Broad Street. The sheet's north arrow sits at the upper right, and the adjoining sheet numbers 3, 5 and 6 are printed around the edges.
notes: Drawn at 200 feet to an inch.
Holdings lettered Henry Lindenmeyer Est., H. O. Van Giesen, T. B. Baxter, S. J. Dodd, B. Coyne, C. Callin, J. R. Gibson, Philip Baum, J. Miller and Beyer Bros.

North end of Glen Ridge at the Montclair line, 200 ft to an inch. Two parts separated by a heavy horizontal line: part 1 (top) Ridgewood Av, Broad St, Bay Av, Oxford St, Essex Av, Forest Av, Sherman Av (W. T. Evans estate, Jarvie and Lindenmeyer estates); part 2 (bottom) Ridgewood Av, Broad St, Watchung Av, Dodd St, Gray St (large estates).

sheet-11-1.description: The upper left part of sheet 11, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and separated from the rest of the sheet by a heavy diagonal line, covers the northwest corner of Glen Ridge along the Montclair line. Glen Ridge Avenue runs diagonally from its junction with Highland and Belleville Avenues near Bloomfield Avenue, which forms the left edge, up to Bay Street at the top. Highland Avenue runs from the same junction up to Bay Street at the right, crossing Argyle Place and the end of Benson Street, and Baldwin Street crosses between Glen Ridge Avenue and Highland Avenue. Along the top, Bay Street meets Grant Street and Sherman Street, which run north into Montclair, and the Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake Division runs north across Bay Street at the upper right. The Montclair town line, with a note to see volume three, crosses the area diagonally. Building is densest along Bloomfield Avenue and Glen Ridge Avenue, where small frame dwellings, a tenement, carpenter shops and stables stand on narrow lots; the lots between Glen Ridge Avenue and Highland Avenue hold larger detached houses, and a Methodist church stands near the Belleville Avenue junction. Mountainside Hospital, with its pavilions and outbuildings, occupies the top right corner beyond the railroad, and a small group of dwellings numbered on Highland Avenue lies just south of it. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are drawn in most streets, with fire alarm boxes at Bay Street and the hospital. A scale bar of 100 feet to an inch and a compass rose are printed in this part.
notes: Glen Ridge Avenue is the modern Glenridge Avenue; Argyle Place is the modern Argyle Street.
Mountainside Hospital at the top right; a Methodist church near Belleville Avenue.
Erie R.R. Greenwood Lake Division runs north across Bay Street; the line is abandoned today (New York and Greenwood Lake Railway in OpenStreetMap).

Highland Av / Glen Ridge Av / Bloomfield Av / Baldwin St / Bay St (Mountainside Hospital), and Sherman Av / Ridgewood Av / Baldwin St. Heavy diagonal line splits the sheet into two parts with their own north arrows: upper left at 100 ft (scale bar), lower right at 50 ft (scale of feet). Erie RR Greenwood Lake Division.

sheet-11-2.description: The lower right part of sheet 11, below a heavy diagonal line, is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. It shows the blocks between Sherman Avenue at the top and Ridgewood Avenue along the bottom edge, ending at Baldwin Street on the right. On the left the Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake Division crosses diagonally on its own right of way towards Ridgewood Avenue, and the dividing line of the sheet runs beside it. The blocks are divided into large suburban lots, most of them still empty. A few detached dwellings stand along Sherman Avenue, two of them marked as being built or partly built, together with stables and a pair of houses on the Ridgewood Avenue frontage, one with a brick first storey and one plastered. A six-inch water pipe is drawn in Sherman Avenue, Baldwin Street and Ridgewood Avenue. The block numbers 5 and 6 and the adjoining sheet numbers 12, 13, 14 and 15 are printed around the edges, and the part has its own scale of feet and north arrow.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch, unlike the upper left part of the sheet (100 feet).

Placed from three points only: Baldwin / Sherman (detected), Baldwin / Ridgewood (hand-picked, centre just off the image) and the crossing of Ridgewood Avenue with the abandoned Erie Greenwood Lake line; low confidence.

Highland Av / Glen Ridge Av / Bloomfield Av / Baldwin St / Bay St (Mountainside Hospital), and Sherman Av / Ridgewood Av / Baldwin St. Heavy diagonal line splits the sheet into two parts with their own north arrows: upper left at 100 ft (scale bar), lower right at 50 ft (scale of feet). Erie RR Greenwood Lake Division.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas covers a thinly built district in the north-west corner of Glen Ridge, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies to the right of the page, as the compass rose and its north arrow show. Highland Avenue runs along the top edge and Essex Avenue along the bottom, with Sherman Avenue, Ridgewood Avenue and Forest Avenue crossing the sheet between them. Baldwin Street forms the left side of the main block, jogging to a new line below Clinton Road, and Bay Avenue runs down the right side. Most of the ground is open or divided into large lots; the buildings are frame dwellings with stables and a few barns, concentrated in a small row on Ridgewood Avenue, along Baldwin Street near Clinton Road and Essex Avenue, and on a block at the lower right behind Bay Avenue. Two tenements and a flats building stand on Highland Avenue near the top. The abandoned Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division crosses the upper left corner on a diagonal passing a large rectangular structure near Highland Avenue. Six-inch water mains are lettered in most streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The borough lines with Montclair at the top right and with Bloomfield at the bottom are drawn as dash-dot lines. The sheet carries its scale bar at the lower left, and adjoining sheets 11, 15, 4 and 7 are numbered in the margins.
notes: The drawn railroad is lettered Erie R.R. Greenwood Lake Div.; it is abandoned today.
Bay is lettered 'BAY' with 'AV.' further along the street, read as Bay Avenue.
A Princeton University Library Map Division stamp crosses the lower right margin.
Highland Av, Sherman Av, Ridgewood Av, Forest Av, Clinton Road, Essex Av, Baldwin St, Bay Av; 100 ft. One part. Turned, north to the right. Configured by helper: 9 points.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas shows the western edge of Glen Ridge at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north lies to the right and slightly up the page, as the compass rose at upper left shows. Highland Avenue runs along the top edge, Sherman Avenue crosses the middle and Ridgewood Avenue runs along the bottom. Belleville Avenue forms the slanting left side of the map, Argyle Place a narrow 50 foot street runs down from Highland Avenue to Sherman Avenue, and Wildwood Terrace, 66 feet wide, runs down the right side between Sherman and Ridgewood avenues. The most important feature is the H. K. & F. S. Benson works, manufacturers of sheet and rolled brass, on the north side of Sherman Avenue at the corner of Belleville Avenue: a rolling mill with a casting room, annealing furnaces, a carpenter shop, a refining and plating room and a metal extracting room, drawn in pink brick and yellow frame, with a printed note on watchman, steam power, coal fuel, gas lights and no fire apparatus. Around it the sheet is largely open lots with scattered frame dwellings, a few larger houses on Belleville Avenue, a group of dwellings and stables on the south side of Sherman Avenue, and a blue-coloured building near the bottom centre. Six-inch and four-inch water mains are lettered in the streets. Hermon Street is lettered as a dashed stub entering Belleville Avenue from the left. The scale of feet is printed at the bottom right.
notes: Argyle Place is today's Argyle Street.
Hermon Street is today's Herman Street.
The works of H. K. & F. S. Benson, Mfr of Sheet & Rolled Brass, with the Rolling Mill, stand at Belleville and Sherman avenues.

Highland Av, Sherman Av, Ridgewood Av, Belleville Av, Argyle Pl, Wildwood Terrace; H. K. & F. S. Benson rolling mill. 50 ft. One part. Turned (rotation about +69). Configured by helper: 7 points; Argyle/Sherman 3.5 m.

sheet-14-1.description: The main part of sheet 14 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right, as the compass rose at the right margin shows. It lies in the north-west of Glen Ridge, between Highland Avenue along the top and Ridgewood Avenue along the bottom edge. Sherman Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet. Argyle Place, a 50 foot street, runs down the left side from Highland Avenue to Sherman Avenue, Benson runs diagonally from Highland Avenue to Sherman Avenue, and Wildwood Terrace, 66 feet wide, runs from Sherman Avenue down to Ridgewood Avenue at the lower left. The Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake Division crosses the sheet from lower left to upper right on a wide right of way, drawn as a bundle of tracks. Most of the ground is divided into lots but only thinly built: a few detached frame dwellings, some plastered, stand on Argyle Place, Highland Avenue and Wildwood Terrace, with a row of three houses at the foot of Wildwood Terrace on Ridgewood Avenue. The triangle between Benson and the railroad is empty apart from one dwelling at its top. Four-inch and six-inch water pipes are lettered in the streets, and the street widths of 50, 60, 66 and 80 feet are noted. Adjoining sheets 11 and 13 are numbered at the margins, and the lower right corner is occupied by an inset, shown as part 2, which is separated by a heavy line.
notes: Argyle Place is today's Argyle Street.
Benson is lettered without a suffix; it appears to be today's Mead Terrace (the modern street lies on the drawn line; not otherwise verified).
The railroad is lettered Greenwood Lake Division, Erie R.R.; the line is abandoned today.
The junction of Wildwood Terrace and Ridgewood Avenue lies at the bottom edge of the image and was not measured.

Highland Av, Sherman Av, Ridgewood Av, Argyle Pl, Wildwood Ter, Benson St, Erie RR Greenwood Lake Division; 50 ft. Inset at lower right behind a heavy line: V. Nevins Church Press on Midland Av (own north arrow), part 2. Part 1 main map (Benson = modern Mead Terrace), 5 points. Part 2 inset (V. Nevins Church Press, Midland Av) placed from four building corners carried from sheet 34; low to medium confidence.

sheet-14-2.description: This inset in the lower right corner of sheet 14 is separated from the main map by a heavy line. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing to the upper right, and shows the works of V. Nevins Church Press, colored printers, on the north side of Midland Avenue in the Glen Ridge and Bloomfield boundary district. The buildings stand in one lot behind Midland Avenue, which crosses the bottom of the inset. They form a long frame range with a press room, rolling room, carton department and office, with wings for folding and cutting, a wax department, a case making room, an imposing department, a tank department and a machine shop. A boiler and engine house with two boilers and a 60 foot chimney, a direct connected engine and dynamos, a well, a water tank of 3,500 gallons, an open coal bin and a shed complete the works. A printed note beside them records a night watchman, steam and electric power, steam heat, electric lights, four Stempel fire extinguishers, water and sand pails, a driven well and a Blake force pump with hose connections. The sheet numbers 34 above, 33 at the left, 11 at the upper left and 43 below are lettered around the inset, and a note says there is no exposure on the left side.
notes: The same buildings are drawn at 100 feet to an inch at the lower left of sheet 34, where they are marked as continuing on another sheet.
Placed only from four building corners carried from sheet 34; there is no street junction in the inset. Low confidence.

Highland Av, Sherman Av, Ridgewood Av, Argyle Pl, Wildwood Ter, Benson St, Erie RR Greenwood Lake Division; 50 ft. Inset at lower right behind a heavy line: V. Nevins Church Press on Midland Av (own north arrow), part 2. Part 1 main map (Benson = modern Mead Terrace), 5 points. Part 2 inset (V. Nevins Church Press, Midland Av) placed from four building corners carried from sheet 34; low to medium confidence.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas covers a lightly built district at the southern edge of Glen Ridge, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies to the right of the page, as the compass rose at left shows. Ridgewood Avenue, 80 feet wide, crosses the top of the sheet, followed down the page by Forest Avenue and Clinton Road, a 50 foot street, with Essex Avenue along the bottom, where the dash-dot line of the borough boundary runs down the middle of the street between Glen Ridge Borough and the Town of Bloomfield. Osborne Street runs down the left side, and Baldwin Street down the right, jogging to a new line below Clinton Road. William Street is lettered at the bottom edge. The blocks are mostly open lots with a scattering of frame dwellings: a row of small houses on the north side of Ridgewood Avenue near the left edge, larger houses with stables facing Forest Avenue and Baldwin Street, an auto house on Forest Avenue, and two pairs of semi-detached houses and a row of dwellings on the north side of Essex Avenue numbered in the 80s and 90s. The Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division crosses the top left corner on a diagonal. Six-inch water mains run in Osborne Street, Clinton Road, Baldwin Street and Essex Avenue. The scale of feet is printed at the lower right; the Princeton University Library Map Division stamp falls on the margin beside it.
notes: Osborne is lettered without a suffix; the modern street is Osborne Street.
The railroad is lettered Erie R.R. Greenwood Lake Div.; the line is abandoned today.
The manual point on Baldwin Street and Ridgewood Avenue was read from the drawn edges because the detector could not find the junction.

Ridgewood Av, Forest Av, Clinton Road, Essex Av, Osborne St, Baldwin St; 50 ft. One part. Configured by helper: 7 automatic points plus a hand-picked Baldwin/Ridgewood at the sheet top; Osborne drawn a few metres off the modern line.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas, titled Bloomfield and Glen Ridge, is a 100 foot to an inch sheet turned so that north lies to the right of the page, as the compass rose at the bottom shows. It covers the boundary district between Glen Ridge and Bloomfield south of Ridgewood Avenue. Ridgewood Avenue runs along the top with a row of dwellings on its south side numbered in the 260s to 290s; Belleville Avenue forms the left side and Osborne Street the right, with Wildwood Terrace, Forest Avenue and Clinton Road crossing the upper part. The Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division, drawn as a bundle of tracks, cuts diagonally across the sheet from top right to lower left, passing a small park and a house lettered Chestnut Hill, Glen Ridge. The centre is largely open ground, much of it Bloomfield Cemetery, crossed by the dash-dot line of the borough boundary between Glen Ridge Borough and the Town of Bloomfield. The lower left is a built-up Bloomfield district along State Street with small lots, shops including a grocery, drug store, meat market and flats; Edgewood Road enters at the left. In the lower right Benson Street and Essex Avenue serve a close-set row of frame dwellings, with a tin shop, and Broad Street runs along the bottom with New Street, Maple Street and Almira Street entering from the north. Six-inch and four-inch water mains are lettered in most streets. Adjoining sheets 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 22 and 23 are numbered around the margin, and the scale bar is at the lower left.
notes: Clinton is lettered Clinton R'd, read as Clinton Road.
The modern node Benson Street / Clinton Road / Wildwood Terrace does not match the drawn junction (18 m off) and was rejected.
The railroad is lettered Erie R.R. Greenwood Lake Division; the line is abandoned today.
Edgewood Road was left out of the control streets (junction with Belleville Avenue 7 m off its modern node).

Ridgewood Av, Belleville Av, Wildwood Ter, Forest Av, Clinton Rd, Osborne St, Benson St, Essex Av, State St, Broad St, High St, Edgewood Road; Bloomfield Cemetery; Erie RR. 100 ft. One part. Configured by helper: 12 points. Edgewood Road left out (junction with Belleville 7 m off); Benson/Clinton/Wildwood rejected (modern merged node, 18 m).

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas shows the works of the Edison Storage Battery Company and the streets around it in the western part of Glen Ridge, at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right, as the compass rose shows. Highland Avenue crosses the top left, with Bloomfield Avenue, an 80 foot street, running down the left side and Belleville Avenue down the right, and Ridgewood Avenue along the bottom. Sherman Avenue is lettered where it ends at Belleville Avenue, and Hermon crosses the lower middle between Bloomfield and Belleville avenues. The Edison works occupy the centre: a large brick factory with assembling, stock and shipping rooms, machine works, a machine shop wing, nickel plating and tin shops, dynamo and engine rooms with three dynamos and three engines, a shed, store room, scrap and oil buildings, a testing house and a wash house, with a printed note on watchman, electric lights, steam heat, coal fuel, hydrants and hose, dry powder fire extinguishers and fire pails. A fire department and police department building with a bell tower, housing a volunteer company, hose wagon and horses, stands on Hermon. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings on lots along Hermon and Belleville Avenue, a livery stable, and open ground, with Park Way lettered as a curved street at the upper left. Six-inch and four-inch water mains, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are shown, and the scale bar is at the bottom right.
notes: Hermon is lettered without a suffix; the modern street is Herman Street.
Park Way is today's Freeman Parkway.
The works are lettered Edison Storage Battery Co.

Only four control points were found (two junctions on Belleville Avenue, Herman at Bloomfield and Belleville, and Ridgewood at Belleville); a hand-picked point at Highland Avenue and Bloomfield Avenue disagreed with the fit and was left out.

Bloomfield Av, Belleville Av, Highland Av, Hermon St, Ridgewood Av, Sherman Av, Park Way; Edison Storage Battery Co. 50 ft. One part. Only 4 control points (Bloomfield/Herman, Belleville/Herman, Belleville/Sherman, Belleville/Ridgewood); low to medium confidence.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas covers the western edge of Glen Ridge and the adjoining Bloomfield line at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper right, as the compass rose near the top shows. Ridgewood Avenue runs along the top, Bloomfield Avenue runs down the left side as an 80 foot street, and Belleville Avenue forms the right side, with a pronounced bend near the middle where it changes direction. Three long streets cross the sheet from left to right: High, 50 feet wide, Hillside Avenue and Edgewood Road, with Park Avenue entering at the lower left. The dash-dot line of the borough boundary between Glen Ridge Borough and the Town of Bloomfield runs along Edgewood Road. The one institution is the Glen Ridge School, a large pink brick building with tile roofs, an arched entrance, assembly room and platform, heated by steam and lit by electricity, with hose connections noted at the stairs. The remaining buildings are frame dwellings: a row of houses on the south side of Ridgewood Avenue, two behind them, and a few near Park Avenue and Edgewood Road. Most of the blocks between High and Edgewood Road are open. Six-inch and four-inch water mains, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are lettered, and the scale bar and the Map Division stamp of Princeton University Library are in the lower right. Neighbouring sheets 21, 24, 26, 17 and 23 are numbered in the margins.
notes: High is lettered without a suffix; the modern street is High Street.
Belleville Avenue is drawn with a bend near the middle that modern Belleville Avenue does not follow, so its junctions with Hillside Avenue and Edgewood Road were left out of the control points.
The junction of Bloomfield, Hillside and Park avenues was excluded as in the lead's notes.

Ridgewood Av, High St, Hillside Av, Edgewood Road, Bloomfield Av, Belleville Av, Park Av; Glen Ridge School. 50 ft. One part. Only 4 control points; Belleville Av drawn with a bend the modern street lacks: its junctions with Hillside and Edgewood excluded; Bloomfield/Hillside excluded.

sheet-24-1.description: The upper part of sheet 24 shows the centre of Bloomfield around the north end of the Green, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and separated by a heavy line from an unrelated block of Glen Ridge below it. It covers the block bounded by State Street at the top, Liberty Street on the left, Broad Street below and Park Street on the right, together with the block between Park Street, Park Avenue, Broad Street and the top of the sheet, and the northern end of the Green itself, lettered as a park between Broad Street and Park Place with Beach Street along its far side. The district is the town's civic and church centre. On the corner of Liberty and State Streets stands the Church of the Sacred Heart (Roman Catholic), with its primary school and rectory, both drawn in pink as brick buildings beside it. The Park Methodist Episcopal Church stands on Park Street near Broad Street, with a parsonage behind it, and the German Presbyterian Church with its manse occupies the corner of State Street and Park Avenue. The remaining lots hold detached frame dwellings, a boarding house on Broad Street, a barn and stables. Water mains of 4, 6 and 12 inches are drawn in the streets, the larger ones along Broad Street and Park Place, and a fire alarm box is marked at the top right corner. The Green is left blank apart from the lettering and the north arrow drawn on it. Adjoining sheets are numbered 26 above State Street, 28 and 46 across Liberty Street, 23 and 48 to the right and 47 below Park Place.
notes: The street lettered Park between State and Broad is the modern Park Street; Park Avenue is the street on the right edge.
Church of the Sacred Heart (R.C.) with its primary school and rectory; Park M.E. Church with parsonage; German Presbyterian Church with manse.
This part is in Bloomfield centre, about 800 m east of part 2 of the same sheet.
Beach / Park Place carried a 3 m residual in the trial fit; the fitted scale is about 2.5 percent below the atlas value, possibly from changes to the streets around the Green.

Two parts separated by a heavy horizontal line. Part 1 (top): Bloomfield centre, State St, Broad St, Liberty St, Park Av, Beach St, Park Pl, the Green ('Park'), Church of the Sacred Heart, Park M.E. Church. Part 2 (bottom): Bloomfield Av, Ridgewood Av, Hillside Av, Snowden Pl, Toneys Brook, D.L.&W. Montclair Branch, Glen Ridge Club. 50 ft.

sheet-24-2.description: The lower part of sheet 24, below a heavy dividing line, shows a block of Glen Ridge between Bloomfield Avenue at the top and Snowden Place at the bottom, with Ridgewood Avenue on the left and Hillside Avenue on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Only the south side of Bloomfield Avenue falls on this part; its north side belongs to other sheets. Toney's Brook winds across the upper half of the block from Ridgewood Avenue to Hillside Avenue, passing under both streets, and below it the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad's Montclair Branch crosses the block diagonally on its own right of way. Most of the ground is still undivided or vacant. The Glen Ridge Club stands on Ridgewood Avenue below the railroad, drawn with its bowling alleys, and beside it are a small auto repairing shop and a gasoline tank. Along the Snowden Place frontage are four detached frame dwellings, and there are a few stables in the interior lots. Water pipes are drawn in Ridgewood Avenue, Hillside Avenue and Snowden Place, and the stub of Woodland Avenue is shown by dashed lines meeting Ridgewood Avenue on the left. Park Avenue is lettered where it leaves the junction of Bloomfield and Hillside Avenues at the top right. A large compass rose sits in the margin to the left of Ridgewood Avenue. Adjoining sheets are numbered 22 above Bloomfield Avenue, 36 across Ridgewood Avenue, 25 across Hillside Avenue and 29 below Snowden Place.
notes: Glen Ridge Club with bowling alleys on Ridgewood Avenue.
D.L.& W. R.R. Montclair Branch crosses the block at grade level in the drawing.
Woodland Avenue is drawn only as a dashed stub.

Placed from few points: two detected junctions and three block corners carried from sheet 29 along Snowden Place; the drawn Bloomfield / Hillside junction disagrees with the modern node by about 10 m and was left out.

Two parts separated by a heavy horizontal line. Part 1 (top): Bloomfield centre, State St, Broad St, Liberty St, Park Av, Beach St, Park Pl, the Green ('Park'), Church of the Sacred Heart, Park M.E. Church. Part 2 (bottom): Bloomfield Av, Ridgewood Av, Hillside Av, Snowden Pl, Toneys Brook, D.L.&W. Montclair Branch, Glen Ridge Club. 50 ft.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right, as the compass rose at the lower left shows. It covers the eastern edge of Glen Ridge where Hillside Avenue meets Bloomfield Avenue, and is crossed from top to bottom by the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad's Montclair Branch, which runs on its own right of way in a long diagonal across the middle. Hillside Avenue runs across the upper part of the sheet from the left edge to Bloomfield Avenue at the right, with Snowden Street entering from the north. Clark curves from Hillside Avenue down the left side, crossing the railroad and continuing to Bloomfield Avenue at the lower right, and Thomas Street is drawn as a dashed water-pipe stub entering Clark from the south. Bloomfield Avenue runs down the right side along the dash-dot line of the boundary between Glen Ridge Borough and the Town of Bloomfield. Toney's Brook winds through the sheet from the top right to the bottom, passing under Hillside Avenue and Clark in boxed culverts. The main works is Tower and Lyon Co., specialties in hardware, between the railroad and the brook, with its machine shop, buffing and packing rooms in a pink brick building, a forging, hardening and rumbling shop in blue, a storage shed and a gasoline tank, and a printed note on power and fire protection. The rest of the sheet is a row of frame dwellings on Hillside Avenue and Clark and long undivided lots. Adjoining sheets 24, 26, 27, 29 and 32 are numbered at the edges.
notes: Snowden Street is today's Snowden Place; Clark is today's Clark Street.

Placed from four junctions only (Hillside with Clark and with Snowden, Clark with Thomas and with Bloomfield Avenue); the Clark and Thomas junction carries a residual of about 3 m and the sheet should be treated as medium to low confidence.
The five-way junction of Bloomfield Avenue, Hillside Avenue and Park Avenue was left out because the drawn junction is about 10 m from the modern nodes.
The Montclair Branch is lettered Delaware, Lackawanna and Western R.R.

Hillside Av, Bloomfield Av, Clark St, Snowden St, Thomas St, Toneys Brook, D.L.&W. RR; Tower & Lyon Co. 50 ft. One part. Only 4 control points; Bloomfield/Hillside five-way junction excluded; Clark/Thomas 3.1 m.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas shows two residential blocks in central Glen Ridge, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet is bounded by Snowden Place at the top, Ridgewood Avenue on the left (west) side, Hillside Avenue on the right (east) side and Appleton Place at the bottom; Clark Street crosses the middle and divides the two blocks. Lincoln Street and Woodland Avenue are only lettered as stubs where they leave Ridgewood Avenue at the left edge. The blocks are given over to large detached dwellings, most of them frame houses with porches, set on deep lots, together with a number of stables and outbuildings at the rear of the lots. The one institution on the sheet is the Glen Ridge Congregational Church on the corner of Ridgewood Avenue and Clark Street, drawn as a frame building with a furnace and electric lighting noted. Water pipes, four-inch mains in most streets, are drawn in Ridgewood Avenue, Hillside Avenue and the cross streets, with hydrants marked at several corners. House numbers are given along the frontages. The surrounding sheets are indicated by their numbers in the margins: 24 above Snowden Place, 25 and 32 beyond Hillside Avenue, 30 below Appleton Place, and 35 and 36 across Ridgewood Avenue. The sheet shows a fully laid out but still partly built-up suburban district, with several lots on each block vacant.
notes: Clark is lettered without a suffix; the modern street is Clark Street.
Glen Ridge Congregational Church at Ridgewood Avenue and Clark.
Snowden Pl, Clark St, Appleton Pl, Ridgewood Av, Hillside Av; Glen Ridge Congregational Church. 50 ft. One part (pilot).

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and covers two blocks of central Glen Ridge, with the north arrow pointing to the upper left. Appleton Place runs along the top of the sheet, Winsor Place crosses the middle and Washington Avenue runs along the bottom, with Ridgewood Avenue, 80 feet wide, down the left edge and Hillside Avenue down the right edge. Hawthorne Avenue enters from the south at the bottom, between Washington Avenue and the sheet below. The upper block, between Appleton Place and Winsor Place, is divided into narrow lots of about 50 feet and is the more built up, with detached frame dwellings, stables and sheds, one drawn in pink as a brick or stone building; the lots on its eastern end, toward Hillside Avenue, are still empty or hold a single house. The lower block, between Winsor Place and Washington Avenue, is mostly open, with deep undivided lots, a few dwellings along Winsor Place, a row of three houses on Ridgewood Avenue near the bottom, and a group of stables and houses on Washington Avenue and near Hillside Avenue. House numbers are given along the frontages. Four-inch and six-inch water pipes run in Ridgewood Avenue, Appleton Place, Winsor Place, Washington Avenue and Hillside Avenue, and the street widths of 50, 60 and 80 feet are noted. Adjoining sheets 29, 31, 32, 34 and 35 are numbered in the margins, and the scale bar and Princeton University Library Map Division stamp are in the lower right.
notes: Washington Avenue is today's Washington Street at this location; Winsor Place and Appleton Place keep their names.
Appleton Pl, Winsor Pl, Washington Av, Ridgewood Av, Hillside Av. 50 ft. One part. Configured by helper: 7 points.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas covers the district where Glen Ridge meets Bloomfield south of Hillside Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Hillside Avenue runs along the top edge. Washington Avenue runs down the left side, curving to the south-east near the bottom, and Winsor Place runs down the right side and then bends south-east to meet Thomas at the lower right corner. Washington Place crosses the middle of the sheet from Washington Avenue to Winsor Place, and the dash-dot line lettered Glen Ridge Borough and Town of Bloomfield runs along it. North of that line the large block between Hillside Avenue and Washington Place holds detached frame dwellings along Washington Avenue and Hillside Avenue and a few houses facing Winsor Place, with a wide undivided tract behind them. South of it the lots fan out around the curve of Washington Avenue, with detached dwellings on the Bloomfield side, one lettered as being built, and an open interior block with a few stables and small buildings. Midland Avenue, Ashland Avenue and Clinton Street enter from the left as dashed water-pipe lines in the margin. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are lettered along Washington Avenue, Washington Place and Winsor Place, with fire alarm boxes at the upper left and lower right. The title Bloomfield and Glen Ridge is printed at the upper left, adjoining sheets 30, 32, 34, 38, 40 and 27 are numbered in the margins, and the scale bar and Map Division stamp are at the bottom.
notes: Washington Avenue is today's Washington Street at this location; Washington Place and Winsor Place keep their names.
Thomas is lettered without a suffix; the modern street is Thomas Street.
Fitted at about 2 m RMSE with a leave-one-out of about 3.5 m; the fitted scale is about 1 percent below the other sheets of the atlas. Medium confidence.

Hillside Av, Washington Av, Washington Pl, Winsor Pl, Thomas St, Midland Av, Ashland Av, Clinton St. 50 ft. One part. Configured by helper: 8 points; Washington Street junctions 2-4 m off, scale about 1 percent low.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right and slightly up the page. It covers a wedge of central Glen Ridge and Bloomfield between Hillside Avenue at the top and Thomas at the bottom, with Winsor Place running down the left side and Clark curving down the right. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad's Montclair Branch crosses the lower right corner on its own right of way, where Clark and Thomas meet beside it. The upper part holds detached frame dwellings with numbered frontages along Hillside Avenue and a row of brick-first-storey houses on Winsor Place, with large undivided lots behind them, one of them marked with a block number. Along Clark, on the right, a row of frame dwellings stands on the inner side of the curve, and a group of stables and sheds lies in the angle behind them. Along Thomas at the bottom a row of detached houses faces the street, numbered in the 150s and 190s. The dash-dot line lettered Glen Ridge Borough and Town of Bloomfield crosses the sheet diagonally from the left margin to the bottom edge. Appleton Place enters Hillside Avenue from the north at the top as a stub with a dashed water pipe, and a stub of Washington Place enters Winsor Place from the left. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and fire alarm boxes are shown, and the scale bar, compass rose and Map Division stamp are in the lower margin. Adjoining sheets 25, 27, 29, 30 and 31 are numbered around the edges.
notes: Clark is lettered without a suffix and Thomas likewise; the modern streets are Clark Street and Thomas Street.
The branch railroad is lettered D.L.& W.R.R. Montclair Branch.

The junction of Clark and Thomas, beside the railroad, was left out of the fit (about 3.5 m residual); five junctions control the part and the leave-one-out error is about 3.5 m, so confidence is medium to low.

Hillside Av, Winsor Pl, Clark St, Thomas St, Washington Pl, Appleton; D.L.&W. Montclair Branch. 50 ft. One part. 5 points; Clark/Thomas beside the railroad excluded; modern Winsor Place bends where the drawn street is straight.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right, as the compass rose at the left shows. It covers the thinly settled western edge of Glen Ridge along the boundary with Montclair and East Orange. At the top Willow Street runs across the sheet from Orange Road, and Cross Street runs down from it to Ridgewood Avenue, 80 feet wide, which crosses the sheet above its middle. Further down Hawthorne Avenue and Oxford Street cross at the right of the sheet, joined by Llewellyn Avenue, with Astor Place entering from the right edge below them, and Midland Avenue runs along the bottom. Orange Road, in Montclair, curves along the upper left edge. Nishuayne Brook runs across the top, and the line of the Town of Montclair, with the note see volume three, and the line of the City of East Orange, crosses the left side. The Glen Ridge Borough and Town of Bloomfield line runs along the bottom. Most of the ground is open or divided into large lots. A few detached frame dwellings, stables and sheds stand on Willow Street and Ridgewood Avenue, and a blue-coloured building lies near Orange Road. A small group of buildings on Midland Avenue includes an iron clad shed and a painting shop, and a few houses and a pink brick building with outbuildings stand on its north side. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are lettered on Orange Road, Ridgewood Avenue and Midland Avenue. Adjoining sheets 34, 14, 43 and 35 are numbered in the margins.
notes: Llewellyn Avenue appears to be today's Adams Place and Oxford Street today's Chapman Place (the modern streets lie on the drawn lines; not otherwise verified).

Placed from five junctions along Cross Street and Llewellyn Avenue only; the junction of Astor Place and Llewellyn Avenue was not detected. The fitted scale is about 1 percent below the atlas value; medium confidence.

Ridgewood Av, Willow St, Cross St, Orange Road, Hawthorne Av, Oxford St, Llewellyn Av, Astor Pl, Midland Av; Toneys Brook; Montclair line. 100 ft. One part. 5 points; Llewellyn Av = modern Adams Place, Oxford St = modern Chapman Place (node positions agree with the drawing).

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 of the 1907 Bloomfield and Glen Ridge atlas is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right, as the compass rose near the right edge shows. It covers the western part of Glen Ridge along the boundary with Montclair and Bloomfield. Ridgewood Avenue crosses the sheet from left to right above its middle and Hawthorne Avenue crosses below it, with Midland Avenue along the bottom edge. Linden Avenue and Maolis Avenue run down the page between them, Llewellyn Avenue forms a narrow street at the left, and Washington Avenue runs down the right side, meeting Hillside Avenue near the lower right corner. Douglas Road and Hamilton Road enter at the upper right corner, and the Montclair town line, with a note to see volume three, crosses the top. The upper blocks are large undivided tracts with scattered frame dwellings and some stables, while the blocks along Hawthorne and Maolis Avenue are mostly open lots with a few dwellings. The one industrial site is the greenhouse range of John Rassbach and Son, florists, on Maolis Avenue at Astor Place, drawn with its boiler room in the cellar and its fuel and hose note; beside it, at the lower left, stand the buildings of the Nevins Church Press, which continue on an inset of sheet 14. Four-inch and six-inch water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are lettered in most streets. The adjoining sheets 33, 35, 30, 31, 37, 38 and 43 are numbered around the edges, and the scale bar is at the lower right.
notes: Llewellyn Avenue appears to be today's Adams Place (the modern street lies on the drawn line; not otherwise verified).
Washington Avenue is today's Washington Street at this location (south of Douglas Road).
John Rassbach and Son, Florists, greenhouses at Maolis Avenue and Astor Place; the Nevins Church Press buildings at the lower left continue on sheet 14.
The junction of Midland Avenue and Washington Avenue was rejected (8.6 m from the fit).

Ridgewood Av, Hawthorne Av, Linden Av, Washington Av, Maolis Av, Llewellyn Av, Astor Pl, Midland Av, Douglas Road, Hamilton Road. 100 ft. One part. 11 points; Midland/Washington rejected (8.6 m); Nevins Church Press and Rassbach greenhouses at lower left.

sheet-35-1.description: The main part of sheet 35, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the residential streets on the west side of Glen Ridge along the Montclair line. Washington Avenue runs down the left side and Lincoln Street down the right; between them Douglas Road and Hamilton Road cross the sheet, with Franklin Place at the top right corner, Summit Street leaving Lincoln Street to the right, and Ridgewood Avenue along the bottom, where Winsor Place, Appleton Place and Clark Street meet it. The Montclair town line, with a note to see volume three, runs across the top. The blocks are laid out in regular suburban lots and are well built up along Douglas Road and Hamilton Road with detached frame dwellings and stables, several of them stuccoed or plastered; the large block between Hamilton Road and Ridgewood Avenue is still mostly open, with a few houses near Lincoln Street. The building of the Glen Ridge Salvage Corps, with eighteen men, stands near the corner of Lincoln Street and Hamilton Road. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn in the streets, with hydrants and a fire alarm box at Lincoln Street and Douglas Road. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad's Montclair Branch crosses the lower left corner just above the heavy line that marks off the inset in the lower left of the sheet. Adjoining sheets are numbered 34, 36, 29 and 30.
notes: Glen Ridge Salvage Corps (18 men) near Lincoln Street and Hamilton Road.
Washington Avenue is today Washington Avenue north of Douglas Road and Washington Street south of it.
The junction of Ridgewood Avenue and Washington Street, beside the railroad, carried a 4 m residual and was left out.

Douglas Road, Hamilton Road, Ridgewood Av, Washington Av, Lincoln St, Franklin Pl, Appleton Pl; 100 ft. Inset at lower left behind a heavy line, 50 ft: Empire Cream Separator Co and Ampere Silk Mill on Nelson St, Willow St, Orange St, D.L.&W. Montclair Branch (part 2).

sheet-35-2.description: The inset in the lower left of sheet 35, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and marked off by a heavy line, shows an industrial block in the Watsessing section of Bloomfield, well south of the Glen Ridge streets on the rest of the sheet. It is bounded by Nelson Street at the top, Willow Street on the left and Orange Street along the bottom, with the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad's Montclair Branch crossing the block diagonally on several tracks and sidings. Above the railroad stands the works of the Empire Cream Separator Company, Henning G. Taube, president: a long brick machine shop with raised sidelights, office, tin shop, packing room, blacksmith shop, engine and dynamo room, a paint shop, a frame store for rough castings, and a long brick building for the storage and assembling of separators running beside the tracks, with open coal bins. A note gives its fire protection: a night watchman, sprinklers in part, an artesian well 110 feet deep and an elevated tank. Below the railroad, on Orange Street, is the Ampere Silk Mill, W. K. Underhill, manager, with weaving rooms, winding and warping rooms, a repair shop, engine and tank rooms, and a dwelling and stables nearby; its note records city water and a fire station opposite. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn in Willow and Orange Streets. The inset has its own north arrow and a scale of 50 feet to an inch, and the block numbers 44 and adjoining sheet number 61 are printed on it.
notes: Empire Cream Separator Co. (Henning G. Taube, Pres.) and Ampere Silk Mill (W. K. Underhill, Mgr.).
Nelson Street is not in the modern street data.

Placed from one hand-picked junction (Orange Street / Willow Street) and a derived point 300 ft along Orange Street at the atlas scale; low confidence. The railroad was grade-separated later and today crosses Orange Street about 12 m north of Willow Street, while the drawing shows it crossing Willow Street, so it was not used for control.

Douglas Road, Hamilton Road, Ridgewood Av, Washington Av, Lincoln St, Franklin Pl, Appleton Pl; 100 ft. Inset at lower left behind a heavy line, 50 ft: Empire Cream Separator Co and Ampere Silk Mill on Nelson St, Willow St, Orange St, D.L.&W. Montclair Branch (part 2).

sheet-36-1.description: The main part of sheet 36, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the centre of Glen Ridge on both sides of Bloomfield Avenue and the railroad. Bloomfield Avenue crosses the top of the sheet diagonally, met by Glen Ridge Avenue, Belleville Avenue, Highland Avenue and Hermon Street; below it Toney's Brook and the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad's Montclair Branch run side by side across the sheet to the Glen Ridge station near Ridgewood Avenue on the right. Park Way crosses the brook and railroad southward to Woodland Avenue. South of Woodland Avenue the residential streets Douglas Road, Hill Crest Road, Summit Street and Marston Place lead down to Lincoln Street along the bottom, with Franklin Place and Hamilton Road at the lower edge, and Ridgewood Avenue runs down the right side past Snowden Place and Clark Street. The Montclair town line, with a note to see volume three, runs down the left margin. Along Bloomfield Avenue are small dwellings and shops, the Capillaris Manufacturing Company and, at the upper left corner, the Acme Laundry, which is drawn in full in the inset at the top of the sheet. Beside the railroad stand the Glen Ridge station, the depot and post office, and a building with offices and the library. The residential blocks hold large detached frame and brick houses on spacious lots, several still vacant. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are drawn in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes at the main corners. Adjoining sheets are numbered 11, 21, 24, 29 and 35.
notes: Modern names: Glen Ridge Avenue is Glenridge Avenue, Park Way is Freeman Parkway, Hill Crest Road is Hillcrest Road, Hermon Street is Herman Street.
Glen Ridge station of the D.L.& W. R.R. Montclair Branch, with depot and post office, and an office and library building.
Capillaris Mfg. Co. and the Acme Laundry on Bloomfield Avenue; the laundry is drawn again at 50 ft in the inset (part 2).

Bloomfield Av, Glen Ridge Av, Belleville Av, Highland Av, Park Way, Woodland Av, Hill Crest Road, Douglas Road, Marston Pl, Summit St, Lincoln St, Ridgewood Av; Toneys Brook, D.L.&W. Montclair Branch, Glen Ridge station. 100 ft. Inset at top behind a heavy box: Acme Laundry on Bloomfield Av (part 2).

sheet-36-2.description: The inset at the top of sheet 36, boxed by a heavy line and drawn at 50 feet to an inch, shows the premises of the Acme Laundry on the south side of Bloomfield Avenue at the Montclair line, the building that the main part of the sheet marks only in outline with a note to see the detached drawing. Bloomfield Avenue, 80 feet wide with a six-inch water pipe, runs across the top of the inset, with the number of the adjoining sheet, 11, beyond it. The laundry, no. 988, is a brick building with an office and flats above at the street front, an ironing room behind and a wash room at the rear, with a frame mangle room and boiler at the side and a frame wagon shed and stable behind it. A small frame building stands to the east, and hydrants are marked on the avenue. The note 'Water facilities' is printed below the avenue, and the left margin carries the reference 'See Vol. 3' for the Montclair side. The inset has its own north arrow, turned about twenty degrees from that of the main part.
notes: Acme Laundry, 988 Bloomfield Avenue.
No street junction: placed by one corner of the laundry carried from the main part of the sheet and a point derived 300 ft along Bloomfield Avenue at the atlas scale; low confidence.

Bloomfield Av, Glen Ridge Av, Belleville Av, Highland Av, Park Way, Woodland Av, Hill Crest Road, Douglas Road, Marston Pl, Summit St, Lincoln St, Ridgewood Av; Toneys Brook, D.L.&W. Montclair Branch, Glen Ridge station. 100 ft. Inset at top behind a heavy box: Acme Laundry on Bloomfield Av (part 2).
